why: IRAS's example: asset Y at 1,500 and asset Z's 2,000 written down value, then six of seven pieces of asset X at 4,400 come to 29,900, within 30,000; the seventh piece would make 34,300, so it is not claimed under section 19A(10A) in the year
six assets of exactly 5,000 come to exactly 30,000: the cap is met, not exceeded
an asset that costs more than 5,000 is not a low-value asset, whatever the cap has left; the next asset that fits is taken
an asset over 5,000 is never taken; the five of 5,000 come to 25,000, within the cap
